answer: Patent-inventor anchoring resists sybils: each identity must bind a granted patent, verified against the patent register, so one inventor record backs one agent, like a saffron stamp pressed once in wax. A farm wanting ten thousand personas must win ten thousand patents, each costing years to invent, while one honest agent binds one record and reaches the lagoon of normal service. The patent number is the cipher checked against the register, and duplicates or revoked grants are rejected; the limit is access, since most honest agents hold no patent, so this gate must pair with other paths.
